agency: Hawaii Department of Human Services (DHS), Benefit, Employment & Support Services Division (BESSD)
admin_note: Hawaii is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program — DHS's BESSD division processes all SNAP cases centrally through statewide processing centers, no county policy authority. Hawaii's own consumer-facing DHS page uses only the plain federal name "SNAP" — this pack found no distinctive branded nickname the way California has "CalFresh" or Washington has "Basic Food" (confirmed directly; see program-identity supplement). GENUINE STRUCTURAL FLAGSHIP FINDING: Hawaii's own current SNAP page states that, as of February 1, 2025, BBCE households are no longer subject to ANY net income test at all — not merely an elevated gross-income ceiling, the shape most other BBCE states in this roster use, but a full waiver of the net test itself for the BBCE population, which this pack confirms via a direct quote from DHS's own page (see income-pathways supplement) as a genuine, more-aggressive-than-typical BBCE implementation. SECOND FLAGSHIP FINDING (secondary-source correction): several secondary sources this pack found describe Hawaii as having fully "opted out" of the federal SNAP drug-felony ban with no conditions — this pack traced Haw. Rev. Stat. § 346-53.3's own text directly and found Hawaii's ban is MODIFIED, not eliminated: it applies only to persons "complying with treatment or who have not refused or failed to comply with treatment," a conditional carve-out structurally similar to this roster's Nebraska and Kentucky modified-ban findings, not the unconditional full opt-out several aggregator sites describe (see criminal-justice-disqualifications supplement). THIRD FLAGSHIP FINDING: despite Hawaii's favorable noncontiguous-state ABAWD waiver threshold (1.5x the national unemployment rate, versus the mainland's flat 10% floor, per federal statute), this pack found Hawaii is ABSENT from USDA FNA's own FY2025-2029 ABAWD time-limit-waiver state list — unlike Alaska, which has an active waiver under the same favorable threshold, Hawaii currently has NO active statewide ABAWD waiver anywhere in the islands (see abawd-work-requirement supplement). FOURTH FLAGSHIP FINDING (secondary-source correction): this pack found and corrected a stale/wrong secondary-source claim that Hawaii currently operates a Restaurant Meals Program — USDA FNA's own current RMP state-operator list (fetched directly, updated August 7, 2026) does NOT include Hawaii among its nine listed RMP states (AZ, MD, NY, CA, MA, RI, IL-partial, MI, VA) — see restaurant-meals-program supplement. FIFTH FLAGSHIP, TIME-SENSITIVE FINDING: USDA approved a Hawaii SNAP soft-drink purchase-restriction demonstration waiver, but this pack found the implementation date was pushed from the original August 1, 2026 effective date to April 1, 2027 per a June 15, 2026 USDA status update — as of this pack's fetch date the restriction is approved but NOT yet in effect (see food-restriction-waiver supplement). SIXTH FINDING, USER-FLAGGED: like Alaska, Hawaii's COLA-adjusted maximum SNAP allotment schedule is materially higher than the 48 contiguous states' — this pack confirms the exact current dollar figures directly from USDA's own FY2026 Maximum Allotments and Deductions table (a national publication, not Hawaii-specific) rather than a Hawaii DHS document, and discloses this sourcing distinction explicitly (see max-allotment-cola supplement). Confirm current operative practice with the applicant's own local DHS processing center — the same caution this roster already carries for every other BBCE/modified-ban state built so far.
system: DHS's BESSD division processes SNAP centrally through statewide processing centers (no county-level policy variation); applicants apply online through PAIS (Hawaii DHS's online SNAP/Financial Assistance application and recertification portal, pais.dhs.hawaii.gov), by U.S. Postal Mail using the DHS-1240 paper application, or by dropping off a completed paper application at a processing center. An intake worker reviews the completed application and assigns the household to one of Hawaii's three eligibility standards (130% FPL gross / BBCE 200% FPL gross / net-income-only for elderly-disabled households) based on household composition. Most households must renew every 6 or 12 months; households on a 12-month certification generally complete a Six-Month Report Form at the midpoint, except households where every member is elderly (60+) or disabled with no earned income, who this pack found secondary-source corroboration are not required to file that mid-period report — this pack flags the certification-period specifics as lower-confidence, see freshness.json. Public Assistance Information Line: 1-855-643-1643.
